data.text: Investigate will ddflow be notified if another agent holding a file and merge (or ddflow itself) will notify an agent that waits to modify this file? If not implement this feature, to support some sort of waking up and minimize the need of human interaction

data.body: Operator 2026-09-29 asked whether an agent blocked on another agent's files is woken when the holder merges. Investigation: no. A refused claim / 'next' conflict leaves the waiter to poll or a human to re-prompt; nothing records who waits, and the holder is never told. Scope: (a) services/waits.py: a local waiter registry (.ddflow/local, pid+deadline liveness) and a poll loop over EventLog.extent() (stat-cheap) that re-plans only when the log grew; (b) api wait(item|phase, timeout, poll): exit 0 when the item (or anything) becomes claimable, naming what freed it; exit 2 on timeout, or immediately when waiting cannot help (cycle, nothing in flight, item done/abandoned); (c) holder side: heartbeat/release/merge/complete name live waiters and the items the release unblocks; (d) CLI 'ddflow wait' + MCP ddflow_wait (bounded timeout); refusals from claim/next point at it; (e) Claude Code delta: run 'ddflow wait' with run_in_background so the harness re-invokes the agent when it exits. Surface wiring (cli.py, mcp.py, api/__init__.py, help.py, driver, README) is held by B16 and is added by widening this item's globs once B16 releases.

data.claim: No: on main 5d71829 ddflow has no notification, wait or subscription path. A blocked agent learns of a release only by re-asking (next/claim); the only guidance is a blind timed wake-up (implement.md: 'a delayed wake-up, not a stop'; Claude Code delta: sleep 600 + ScheduleWakeup). Nothing records who waits, so the holder is never told.
data.falsifier: Any verb or MCP tool that blocks until a lease/dependency clears, or any code path that pushes to/records a waiting agent.
data.mechanism: Leases are events; release/complete append lease.released/item.completed to .ddflow/events and return. No code reads the log on behalf of a waiter, and there is no waiter registry.
data.probe: git grep -niE 'notif|wake|waiter|wait_for|subscribe' main -- ddflow (minus MCP notifications/initialized); ddflow --help | grep wait
data.probe_output: Only hits: claude-code.md delta (ScheduleWakeup / sleep 600 heartbeat) and implement.md ('waiting on another agent's lease ... a delayed wake-up, not a stop'). No verb matches 'wait' except 'job' help text. leases.release appends lease.released and returns.
data.question: Is an agent blocked on another agent's lease (glob conflict or dependency) ever notified when the holder merges/completes/releases, and is the holder ever told someone waits?

**Severity: low — `claim`'s "wait" hint is emitted for an EXPIRED lease, where `wait` refuses immediately**

- Location: `ddflow/api/lifecycle.py:607` (hint appended whenever `exc.holder` is set and differs from the claimant), versus the expired-lease branch at `ddflow/api/lifecycle.py:179`.
- CONFIRMED (reproduced): after a 1 s TTL expires, `claim T1` by another agent exits 3 and appends `Or 'ddflow wait --item T1': it sleeps until holder lets go and returns the moment the item can be claimed.` But `wait --item T1` returns exit 2 at once: "Not waiting: T1's lease from holder has expired and is not handed on automatically … `ddflow recover --item T1`".
- Concrete harm: the refusal promises sleeping behaviour the code does not implement (and the project has shipped docstring/behaviour mismatches before), costing the caller a wasted round trip.
- Suggested fix: only append the `wait` hint for the live-holder and glob-conflict refusals, or word it so the expired-lease case points at `ddflow recover` instead.
